newsitem.title: CHILE: Endesa, CMS to build Chile plants.
newsitem.headline: Endesa, CMS to build Chile plants.

text.p: Empresa Nacional de Electricidad SA (Chile) and CMS Energy Corp will jointly build three 200-MW power plants in northern Chile, the companies said Thursday.
The plants will be powered with natural gas from the Atacama natgas pipeline, which the two companies plan to build over the Andes from the northern Argentine province of Salta, they said.
All three plants will be in the port of Mejillones, near Antofagasta. Two will come into operation in early 1999 and the third in early 2000.
The cost of all three plants will be $300 million, the companies said in a statement.
The two firms have been receiving contracting bids to build the plants since December, and bids will be received until March 3. Bid winners likely will be announced in April.
The announcement was the latest step in a growing competition between two major projects to supply power to northern Chile's booming copper industry.
The Atacama project, due to be finished in 1999, proposes to bring Argentine natural gas over the Andes via a pipeline.
A rival project by power generator Chilgener, known as ElectroAndes, calls for building a 600 MW plant in Salta plus power transmission lines to Chile.

The rivalry resembles in some ways that between two natural gas projects, GasAndes and Transgas, which both proposed to build pipelines over the southern Andes. So far only GasAndes is being built. It is due to come into operation early next year.
As with the GasAndes-Transgas rivalry, energy analysts say demand is not strong enough to justify building both Atacama and ElectroAndes.
The Endesa-CMS pipeline will cost about $350 million.
